source.title: Building the System
source.summary: What an Islamic monetary system would look like, not at the bank level, but at the system level. Principles, obstacles, and the path forward.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Gold dinar revival proposals sound appealing but face practical limitations. This episode moves beyond nostalgia to ask what a modern Islamic monetary system would actually require: five design principles for an Islamic monetary authority, the question of OIC monetary cooperation, and why governance is the binding constraint, not monetary design. The principles exist, the capital exists, the technology exists, and the need is real. But building institutions requires the hardest thing of all: trust between governments that have rarely cooperated at this level.

The principles exist. The capital exists. The technology exists. What's missing is trust between governments that have rarely cooperated at this scale.
Building an Islamic monetary system isn't a monetary design problem. It's an institutional problem. Five design principles exist for an Islamic monetary authority.

The real question isn't whether OIC monetary cooperation is possible. It's whether governments can build the institutions that make cooperation work. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-6

linkedin.post: The conversation around Islamic monetary systems often focuses on technical details—gold standards, currency baskets, or Shariah compliance frameworks. But the real challenge lies elsewhere entirely. Gold dinar revival proposals face a binding constraint that has nothing to do with monetary design. The principles exist. The capital exists. The technology exists. The need is demonstrably real across the Islamic world. What's missing is something much harder to engineer: trust between governments that have rarely cooperated at this institutional scale. Building an Islamic monetary system isn't fundamentally a monetary problem—it's a governance problem. Five clear design principles exist for an Islamic monetary authority. The question of OIC monetary cooperation has technical solutions. But creating the institutions that make sustained cooperation work between sovereign nations remains the ultimate challenge. Listen to the full discussion: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-6
